tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

In a worktree the fork gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip: commit first (uncommitted edits stay here). Bold title line and one sentence right before the call; after it, stop that task here and answer the new message — no recap.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). #!/bin/bash
# usage: axcheck.sh Module.Name [Module.Name ...]   (run after lake build of those modules)
SP=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/ref
F=$SP/axcheck_$$.lean
{
  echo "import Lean"
  for m in "$@"; do echo "import $m"; done
  echo 'open Lean Elab Command in'
  echo '#eval show Lean.Core.CoreM Unit from do'
  echo '  let env ← getEnv'
  printf '  for modName in [%s] do\n' "$(printf '`%s, ' "$@" | sed 's/, $//')"
  cat <<'L'
    let some mod := env.getModuleIdx? modName | throwError "no module"
    let mut all := 0
    let mut thms := 0
    let mut bad : Array (Name × Array Name) := #[]
    for (n, ci) in env.constants.map₁.toList do
      if env.getModuleIdxFor? n == some mod then
        all := all + 1
        if let .thmInfo _ := ci then thms := thms + 1
        let axs ← collectAxioms n
        let extra := axs.filter fun a => a != ``propext && a != ``Quot.sound
        if !extra.isEmpty then bad := bad.push (n, extra)
    IO.println s!"{modName}: constants {all}, theorems {thms}"
    IO.println s!"outside propext, Quot.sound: {bad}"
L
} > $F

241	theorem r6_path {Ty : Type} {k : K} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
242	    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {π : Params Ty} (hπ : ParamsOK C π) {s3 s3' : S3}

244	    ∀ {s2 : Machine.State}, (∀ q ∈ t, WF3 q.2 ∧ NoDangling q.2) → KObl k C ObR ObW π t s2 →
245	      Refinement.Repr π.L π.rtok s3 s2 →
246	      Machine.Exec C ObR ObW (ktrace π t s2) s2 (run s2 (ktrace π t s2)) ∧
247	        Refinement.Repr π.L π.rtok s3' (run s2 (ktrace π t s2)) := by
248	  induction hp with
249	  | nil => intro s2 _ _ hR; exact ⟨.nil _, hR⟩
250	  | cons h _ ih =>
251	    intro s2 hinv hob hR
252	    obtain ⟨hw, hnd⟩ := hinv _ (List.mem_cons_self ..)
253	    obtain ⟨hob₁, hob₂⟩ := hob
254	    obtain ⟨hex, hR₁⟩ := r6 hπ hR hw hnd h hob₁
255	    obtain ⟨hex', hR'⟩ := ih (fun q hq => hinv q (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hq)) hob₂ hR₁
256	    simp only [ktrace]
257	    rw [run_append]
258	    exact ⟨exec_append hex hex', hR'⟩

357	  | @ok E' s₁ s₂ hE' _ _ hsp hst =>

521	      SimRun k C ObR ObW statics π s3' (run s2 (ktrace π t s2)) := by
522	  induction hp with
523	  | nil => intro s2 h _ _; exact h
524	  | cons h _ ih =>
525	    intro s2 hs hinv hob
526	    obtain ⟨hw, hnd⟩ := hinv _ (List.mem_cons_self ..)
527	    obtain ⟨hob₁, hob₂⟩ := hob
528	    have := ih (SimRun.step hs hw hnd h hob₁) (fun q hq => hinv q (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hq))
529	      hob₂

540	  induction h with
541	  | init hst hlay hob => exact SimRun.init hst hlay hob
542	  | step _ hw hnd hs hob ih => exact simRun_path (kexp_path hs) ih (kexp_inv hs hw hnd) hob

575	state it starts from. -/
576	inductive LPath (k : K) : LState → List (LOp × LState) → LState → Prop where
577	  | nil (L : LState) : LPath k L [] L
578	  | cons {lop : LOp} {L L₁ L' : LState} {t : List (LOp × LState)} :
579	      LOpStep k lop L L₁ → LPath k L₁ t L' → LPath k L ((lop, L) :: t) L'

587	theorem ltrace_append (t t' : List (LOp × LState)) : ltrace (t ++ t') = ltrace t ++ ltrace t' := by
588	  induction t with
589	  | nil => rfl
590	  | cons p t ih =>
591	    obtain ⟨lop, L⟩ := p
592	    simp only [List.cons_append, ltrace, ih, List.append_assoc]

597	  induction hp with
598	  | nil => exact .cons hs (.nil _)
599	  | cons h _ ih => exact .cons h (ih hs)

603	    ∀ (t₁ : List (LOp × LState)) {L₀ : LState}, LPath k L₀ (t₁ ++ (lop, L) :: t₂) L₂ →
604	      ∃ L₁, LOpStep k lop L L₁ ∧ LPath k L₁ t₂ L₂
605	  | [], _, h => by
606	    cases h with
607	    | cons hs hp => exact ⟨_, hs, hp⟩
608	  | (_, _) :: t₁, _, h => by
609	    cases h with
610	    | cons _ hp => exact LPath.split t₁ hp

612	/-- The machine trace of a translated library run is the trace of its kernel steps (§82.7): the

618	    ∃ t, LPath k (LState.init statics) t L ∧
619	      s2 = run (minit π statics) (ktrace π (ltrace t) (minit π statics)) := by
620	  induction h with
621	  | init => exact ⟨[], .nil _, rfl⟩
622	  | step _ _ _ hs _ ih =>
623	    obtain ⟨t, hp, rfl⟩ := ih
624	    refine ⟨_, hp.snoc hs, ?_⟩
625	    rw [ltrace_append, ktrace_append, run_append]

629	/-- The authority that a kernel step uses as a means of access (§82.7): the authority through
630	which `read`, `write` and `writeShared` access leaves (§66.2, §67.1, §68.2), the authority whose

632	means of access (§60.1, §61.1). The other operations use none. -/
633	def usedAuth : KOp → Option Nat
634	  | .read a _ => some a
635	  | .write a _ _ => some a
636	  | .writeShared a _ _ => some a
637	  | .store a _ => some a
638	  | .derive src _ _ => some src
639	  | .split src _ => some src
640	  | _ => none

642	/-- An authority exercisable at some mode is active (§43). -/
643	theorem active_of_exercisable {s : S3} {a : Nat} {m : Mode} (h : s.ExercisableAt a m) :
644	    s.Active a := by
645	  cases h with
646	  | base hy ha => exact ⟨_, hy, ha⟩
647	  | held hy ha => exact ⟨_, hy, ha⟩
648	
649	/-- A kernel step uses only an active authority (§60.1, §61.1, §65.1, §66.2, §67.1, §68.2). -/
650	theorem usedAuth_active {k : K} {op : KOp} {s s' : S3} {j : Nat} (h : OpStep k op s s')
651	    (hv : usedAuth op = some j) : s.Active j := by
652	  cases op with
653	  | read a ls =>
654	    obtain rfl : a = j := Option.some.inj hv
655	    exact active_of_exercisable (Guarded.ok_iff.1 h).1.exercisable
656	  | write a ls w =>
657	    obtain rfl : a = j := Option.some.inj hv
658	    exact active_of_exercisable (Guarded.ok_iff.1 h).1.exercisable
659	  | writeShared a ls w =>
660	    obtain rfl : a = j := Option.some.inj hv
661	    exact active_of_exercisable (Guarded.ok_iff.1 h).1.exercisable
662	  | store a p =>
663	    obtain rfl : a = j := Option.some.inj hv
664	    have hd := (Guarded.ok_iff.1 h).1.derivedHeld
665	    unfold OptP at hd
666	    split at hd
667	    · exact ⟨_, ‹_›, hd.1⟩
668	    · exact hd.elim
669	  | derive src r m =>
670	    obtain rfl : src = j := Option.some.inj hv
671	    exact (Guarded.ok_iff.1 h).1.active
672	  | split src rs =>
673	    obtain rfl : src = j := Option.some.inj hv
674	    exact (Guarded.ok_iff.1 h).1.active
675	  | transfer => cases hv
676	  | release => cases hv
677	  | depend => cases hv
678	  | enter => cases hv
679	  | exit => cases hv
680	  | pin => cases hv
681	  | unpin => cases hv
682	  | endUse => cases hv
683	  | free => cases hv
684	  | alloc => cases hv

688	theorem lpath_unused {k : K} {s₀ : S3} {j : Nat} (hj : j < s₀.A.length) (hd : ¬ s₀.Active j)
689	    {L L₂ : LState} {t : List (LOp × LState)} (hp : LPath k L t L₂) :
690	    AKeep s₀ L.kern → ∀ q ∈ ltrace t, usedAuth q.1 ≠ some j := by
691	  induction hp with

696	    rcases hq with hq | hq

698	      exact hd ((hk.trans hk').active_back (usedAuth_active hst hv) hj)
699	    · exact ih (hk.trans (lstep_akeep hs.lstep)) q hq hv

701	/-- No access after invalidation (§82.7, §78, §86): after a legal `reset` of entry `i`, along
702	every continuation of the library run, no kernel step reads, writes or writes in shared mode
703	through, stores, or derives or splits from an authority derived from `internal` that covered a
704	leaf of the administered storage; so none of the raw operations of the continuation realizes an
705	access through it. -/
706	theorem reset_no_access {k : K} {L L₁ L₂ : LState} {i : Nat} {E : ArenaEntry}
707	    {t : List (LOp × LState)} (hE : L.arenas[i]? = some E) (hr : ResetD i L (.ok L₁))

710	    ∀ q ∈ ltrace t, usedAuth q.1 ≠ some j := by
711	  have hjL : j < L.kern.A.length := by

714	    | none => simp [S3.afp, hlj] at hl
715	    | some _ => exact lt_of_getElem? hlj
716	  exact lpath_unused ((lstep_akeep (k := k) (.reset hr)).lt hjL) (reset_ends_covering hE hr hj hc)

720	live entry satisfying `EntryInv`, after a legal `reset`, along every continuation of the library
721	run, no kernel step uses a block issued before the reset on a nonempty region. -/
722	theorem reset_no_access_issued {k : K} {L L₁ L₂ : LState} {i : Nat} {E : ArenaEntry}
723	    {t : List (LOp × LState)} (hE : L.arenas[i]? = some E) (hinv : EntryInv L.kern E)

735	/-- §82.7 for translated library runs: the kernel steps of the derived operations are realized
736	by O1–O16 without reintroducing access after invalidation. The run is a labelled library run from
737	the initial library state; its memory state is reached from the initial memory state by the raw
738	operations of its kernel steps (the machine trace of the run is the trace of its kernel steps);
739	and after every legal `reset` in the run, no kernel step of the continuation uses an authority

744	realization in this model, so the "metadata" part of §82.7 is not covered. This is a reading,

748	storage updated by `writeShared`, provider metadata, the leaves of the arena value), which would

751	    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {statics : Statics} {π : Params Ty} {L : LState}

758	          ∀ q ∈ ltrace t₂, usedAuth q.1 ≠ some j := by
759	  obtain ⟨t, hp, hs⟩ := h.trace
760	  refine ⟨t, hp, hs, ?_⟩
761	  rintro t₁ t₂ L₀ i E rfl hE j hj hc
762	  obtain ⟨L₁, hr, hp₂⟩ := LPath.split t₁ hp
763	  exact reset_no_access hE hr hp₂ hj hc

765	/-! ## A concrete library run (non-vacuity; §82.7, Part XIV) -/
766	
767	section Dec
768	
769	variable (k : K) [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable]
770	  [DecidablePred k.Pinned] [DecidablePred k.ExternalDone] [DecidablePred k.Deallocable]
771	  [∀ p a, Decidable (k.FreeCompat p a)] [∀ p ls s, Decidable (k.Satisfiable p ls s)]
772	  {Ty : Type} (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) [DecidableRel C] (ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty)
773	  (ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty) [∀ s o, Decidable (Obl ObR ObW s o)] (π : Params Ty)

779	  | (op, s3) :: t, s2 =>
780	    @instDecidableAnd _ _ (stepOblDec k C ObR ObW π op s3 s2) (kOblDec t _)

788	/-- Memory state after the library operations `t`, each listed with the library state it starts
789	from, from the memory state `m` (§82.7). -/

799	  | (lop, L) :: t, m => by
800	    rw [lrunM, lrunM_eq π t, ltrace, ktrace_append, run_append]
801	    rfl

803	/-- A library run through every derived arena operation (Part XIV, §76–§78; the states of
804	`Arena.Witness`): `derive(1, [1], Modify)` and `store(3, 0)` prepare `internal` 3 held by the arena
805	value 0; `newArena(1, 3)`; `issue(0, [1], 2)` (block 4 stored into 2); `write(4, [1])`;
806	`endUse(2)`; `reset(0)`; `issue(0, [1], 2)` again (block 6). -/
807	def tA : List (LOp × LState) :=
808	  [(.kernel (.derive 1 [1] .modify), Witness.w0), (.kernel (.store 3 0), Witness.w1),
809	   (.newArena [] 1 3, Witness.w2), (.issue 0 [1] 2, Witness.w3),
810	   (.kernel (.write 4 [1] wv), Witness.r4), (.kernel (.endUse 2), Witness.r5),
811	   (.reset 0, Witness.r6), (.issue 0 [1] 2, Witness.r7)]
812	
813	/-- Parameters of the run, fixed once (§82): the test layout of the three static places. -/
814	def πA : Params Unit := piOf (S3.init st).P []

816	/-- Final memory state of the run (§82.7). -/
817	def finA : Machine.State := lrunM πA tA (minit πA st)

820	a state satisfying `WF3` and `NoDangling`, is an `ok` library step, and its kernel steps satisfy
821	their obligations under the fixed parameters. -/

823	  have h0 : LSimRun K0 (· = ·) obR obW st πA Witness.w0 (minit πA st) :=
824	    .init (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)
825	  have h1 := LSimRun.step (lop := .kernel (.derive 1 [1] .modify)) (L' := Witness.w1) h0
826	    (wf3_of_check (by decide)) (noDangling_of_check (by decide)) ⟨.ok (by decide), rfl⟩
827	    (by decide)
828	  have h2 := LSimRun.step (lop := .kernel (.store 3 0)) (L' := Witness.w2) h1
829	    (wf3_of_check (by decide)) (noDangling_of_check (by decide)) ⟨.ok (by decide), rfl⟩
830	    (by decide)
831	  have h3 := LSimRun.step (lop := .newArena [] 1 3) (L' := Witness.w3) h2
832	    (wf3_of_check (by decide)) (noDangling_of_check (by decide)) (.ok (by decide)) (by decide)
833	  have h4 := LSimRun.step (lop := .issue 0 [1] 2) (L' := Witness.r4) h3
834	    (wf3_of_check (by decide)) (noDangling_of_check (by decide))
835	    (IssueD.ok (E := Witness.wE) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (.ok (by decide))
836	      (.ok (by decide))) (by decide)
837	  have h5 := LSimRun.step (lop := .kernel (.write 4 [1] wv)) (L' := Witness.r5) h4
838	    (wf3_of_check (by decide)) (noDangling_of_check (by decide)) ⟨.ok (by decide), rfl⟩
839	    (by decide)
840	  have h6 := LSimRun.step (lop := .kernel (.endUse 2)) (L' := Witness.r6) h5
841	    (wf3_of_check (by decide)) (noDangling_of_check (by decide)) ⟨.ok (by decide), rfl⟩
842	    (by decide)
843	  have h7 := LSimRun.step (lop := .reset 0) (L' := Witness.r7) h6
844	    (wf3_of_check (by decide)) (noDangling_of_check (by decide))
845	    (ResetD.ok (E := Witness.rE) (by decide) (.ok (by decide)) (.ok (by decide)) (by decide))
846	    (by decide)
847	  exact LSimRun.step (lop := .issue 0 [1] 2) (L' := Witness.r8) h7
848	    (wf3_of_check (by decide)) (noDangling_of_check (by decide))
849	    (IssueD.ok (E := Witness.rE') (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (.ok (by decide))

852	/-- Non-vacuity of the library simulation (§82.7, §82.3): the run is translated into an execution
853	of `ok` raw steps from the empty state, `Repr` holds at its end, the final library state is
854	library-reachable, and the machine trace is the trace of the kernel steps. The reference written
855	into the arena value 0 and the one written into the destination 2 by the second issue decode to
856	the address of the storage leaf 1, which is nonzero and whose allocation is live. The range of

858	designates the former value in the memory machine too (no rule of §77 or §78 changes these bytes;
859	see `Arena.Witness.reissue_reads_former_value` for §86). -/
860	theorem runA_sim :
861	    ((∃ ops, Machine.Exec (· = ·) obR obW ops Machine.State.empty finA) ∧
862	      Refinement.Repr πA.L πA.rtok Witness.r8.kern finA ∧ LReach K0 st Witness.r8) ∧
863	    finA = run (minit πA st) (ktrace πA (ltrace tA) (minit πA st)) ∧

865	    leafAddr finA πA.L 1 ≠ 0 ∧ (finA.allocs (πA.L 1).alloc).map (·.live) = some true ∧
866	    ∀ n < 8, bytesOf finA πA.L 1 n = wv 1 n :=
867	  ⟨lsimulation (piOf_ok _ []) runA_lsim, lrunM_eq _ _ _, by decide, by decide, by decide,
868	    by decide, by decide⟩

# ERN — Memory Model Specification v0.1

**Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated**

Modified clauses, relative to v0 (each change is justified by a defect found while formalizing v0):

- §36: `MetaRight` governs authorities over existing storage, not the fresh allocation of `alloc`; §36 and §71.2 contradicted each other.
- §40: `RootHeld` restricted to usable root places, as in §49.7; the two clauses differed on unusable root places.
- §47: the ownership graph of statics is acyclic; a static ownership cycle made §57 false in the initial state.
- §51: a valid origin is an active origin; "valid" was undefined there.
- §57: definition of I5, which v0 named without defining.
- §59: "access operations" are O9–O11; read as all operations, §59 contradicted §69.
- §60.1: a valid origin chain is an active one, read through §44.
- §63.4: the active derived authorities covering the source from outside are named, and the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right are exempt; without this exemption no value could be moved through a derived authority.
- §63.9 (new): the destination is usable in the resulting state; without it an accepted transfer could create an ownership cycle and break §49.8 and §57.
- §69.2 and §70.3: the same exemption as §63.4, and rejection when an authority made inactive by the step keeps an active descendant; without it an accepted step left an active authority with an inactive origin.
- §71.2: the provider is a usable place; v0 did not require it to exist.
- §74 and §75: each `pin` installs an obligation of fresh identity and `unpin` ends one designated obligation; per-leaf pin flags let an `unpin` lift a pin installed by another `pin`.
- §76.6: the reading of the precondition (whole kernel state, `ArenaInv` of the new entry, resulting state); v0 admitted several readings with different verdicts.
- §78.3: restricted to anchors covering a leaf of the administered storage; as written, its second sentence was false.
- §82.2: address and provenance of a pointer to a region whose leaves all have zero physical size; v0 decided no address for that region.
- §86: the last sentence is rewritten; as written, it was false, since `reset` and `issue` leave a recycled leaf `Init` and readable.

**Higher normative authority:** *ERN — Language Charter v0* (October 27, 2026).  
This specification defines the normative rules of ERN's memory model. Technical names (`derive`, `transfer`, `issue`, etc.) designate **abstract semantic operations**; they do not constitute syntax decisions.

## Validation and Revision Procedure

This edition has been validated and acquires normative authority under the ERN Charter v0. Any subsequent semantic change must identify the clauses concerned, justify the change, and preserve the guarantees of the ERN Charter v0. Formal models and proofs are instruments for verifying this specification, not sources of additional rules. Behaviors not determined within its scope are explicitly identified.

## Scope

This specification defines:

- the safe-code contract;
- the abstract machine for allocations, bytes, and accesses;
- the second-class access discipline;
- footprints, authorities, dependencies, frames, and ownership;
- read, write, transfer, release, allocation, and pinning transitions;
- the normative contract of arenas as a reference library abstraction;
## 76. O17 — Creation of an Administered Arena

**Preconditions**

1. `storage` is an existing, usable place under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame. It may be local, static, allocated, or a block issued by a previous arena.
2. `internal` is explicitly named by the caller, exists, is active, has own mode `Modify`, and `ExercisableAt(s,internal,Modify)` holds.
3. `internal` is **held by a place**: that place is the arena value; `footprint(internal) = footprint(storage)`.
4. **Unified administration guard (Section 56):** no **live** administrative abstraction, whether an arena or a library instance such as a handle pool, already uses this `internal` identity. The relevant registries of library administrations are consulted before registration. Two distinct identities may cover common leaves: this is not in itself grounds for rejection.
5. All leaves of the arena value holding `internal` are already `Init`; construction does not initialize them implicitly.
6. Dependency, holder, storage, and administration relations respect, in the resulting state, `WF3`, I1, `AnchorOrder`, and `AnchorOrderHeld` over the whole kernel state, and the new entry satisfies `ArenaInv` (Section 55).

**`ok` effect:** A live entry `{storage, internal, available, issued}` is added; the initial `available` set represents the administered storage, and `issued` is initially empty. Registering the entry fabricates no place, access right, or `Init` state. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

The identity of `internal`, not the index of `storage`, is the key to preventing duplication of live administrations. No global constraint requires footprints of live arenas to be pairwise disjoint.

## 77. O18 — Issuing an Arena Block

**Static preconditions**

1. The `arena` entry exists and is live; `internal` is active. `MetaRight` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value holding `internal` (Section 36). Mutation of metadata through `writeShared` alone does not satisfy this condition.
2. `region` belongs to the administered storage; `destination` is a usable **leaf** holding no active authority; the destination can legally receive the block value in mode `Modify`. The fact that `destination` is already `Init` is not in itself grounds for rejection, in accordance with O8.2.
   **Local self-blocking prevention: leaf `destination` is not in `region`, including when the region is declared available.** This condition is static and is checked before an availability `fail`.
3. Applicable **static** validity and non-escape restrictions for the destination are satisfied. The `AnchorOrder` check depending on the new anchor is performed on the **simulated resulting state**, after the availability check described in point 4; it cannot turn an unavailable issuance (`fail`) into `reject`.

**Availability and exercisability checks**

4. If static conditions hold but **at least one leaf of `region` does not belong to `available`**, the operation produces **`fail` and leaves the entire state unchanged**. The empty region is always available. An unavailable region does not permit a prior static rejection to be bypassed.
5. If the region is available, the effective mode of `internal` on that region must permit `Modify`; otherwise the outcome is `reject`.
6. The simulated result must satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` **in the resulting state**; moreover, **in that resulting state, `destination` must remain under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame**, in accordance with O8.5. Issuance into a value with a longer lifetime than a local anchor is not made valid merely by storing it in the caller.

**`ok` effect:** A block authority of fresh identity, derived from `internal` and of mode `Modify`, is issued for the region; it is held by `destination`, which receives the corresponding anchor. The leaves of the region leave `available`, and the issuance is added to `issued` with its authority. **Only leaf `destination` becomes `Init`**; no other leaf of the arena value changes initialization. Previous issuances remain intact and valid. Issuance does not automatically install anchors on third-party values: they must use their lawful dependency mechanisms.

**Outcomes:** `ok`, `fail` (region unavailable after static validation), `reject` (static rule, effective right, or anchoring not satisfied). The destination may be a leaf of the arena value itself: its initialization then constitutes **an explicit write to that destination**, not implicit initialization of the entire arena value's metadata.

## 78. O19 — Collective Arena Reset

**Preconditions**

1. The entry exists and is live. **`MetaRight(s,arena)` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value**, in accordance with Section 36. `writeShared` over metadata alone, even when legal, does not replace such exercise. `internal` and the arena's other restrictions remain valid.
2. **No active authority derived from `internal` covers a leaf of the administered storage.** A derived authority with an empty footprint does not, by itself, block `reset`.
3. No still-usable place depends, directly or transitively, on an anchor in the **strict origin subtree of `internal`** (`internal` itself is excluded) that covers a leaf of the administered storage. Under precondition 2 and invariant I3, this condition follows from the absence of active descendants covering the storage, and remains explicit in the abstraction contract. Validity obligations of other nested arenas remain satisfied.

**`ok` effect:** All **leaves** of the administered storage become available again, and the issuance list is cleared under the arena contract. No still-active derived authority covering those leaves may remain, by precondition 2; an empty-footprint derivative may remain active without designating any recycled leaf. **No leaf is made `Init` by `reset`**, including in the arena value. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

Safe reuse after `reset` requires that previous issuances **covering recycled leaves**, and the dependencies on which their validity rests, have effectively ceased preventing their reuse. Any active empty-footprint derivatives cover none of those leaves. A historically issued region does not remain permanently unavailable solely for that reason.

# XV. Transitive Dependencies, Returns, and Value Behavior

Dependent values may survive transfers and calls only if the required anchors and rights remain valid. Second-class access does not imply an arbitrary persistent reference.

## 79. Non-Escaping Values and Returns

The second-class nature of access authorities does not prohibit constructing a value carrying a derived authority or returning a result dependent on a caller-owned resource. What is prohibited is artificially extending the validity of a local origin.

A typical scenario is:

```text
arena = create_arena()
buffer = create_buffer(arena)
use(buffer)
endUse(buffer)       // or equivalent release of its dependent rights
arena.reset()
```

The scenario is permitted when:

1. the call receives and exercises valid authorities over the arena;
2. issuance supplies a block disjoint from live issuances;
3. the result value is anchored to the rights actually required;
4. its transfer to the caller respects `SameShape`, holders, `AnchorOrder`, and `AnchorOrderHeld`;
5. `exitFrame` can reanchor surviving authorities without using a dead local root;
6. `reset` is rejected while the dependent result or a block authority remains active, then becomes permitted after those rights have effectively ended.

A “non-escaping” value is therefore not necessarily confined to the frame in which it was created. It may survive a function when it depends on a caller anchor, without extending dead local storage. This result does **not** imply strong protection of all parameter authorities throughout the entire invocation: the historical interpretation of reborrows and this property are deferred to Spec 3.

Properties of transfer between threads and shareability do not follow from this sequential model alone. They depend on external resources, contained authorities, anchors, confinement restrictions, and the concurrency model of Spec 2.

# XVI. External Contracts and Interfaces with Other Specifications

Declarative contracts create no rights. Their satisfaction is an obligation of the language, typing, implementation, or a safe abstraction, according to the nature of each contract.

## 80. Parametric Contracts of the Access Discipline
## 82. Representation Relation and Concrete Obligations

1. **Places and bytes:** relate `P`, `footprint` leaves, their ownership, and their parts to the storage units, offsets, ranges, identities, and alignment constraints of the elementary memory machine; establish actual disjointness for `DeclaredDisjoint` declarations.
2. **Authorities and operations:** connect effective modes and `ExercisableAt` to concrete read, write, and pointer-validity conditions; show that safe access governed by Parts VI through XV satisfies the obligations of Part III, without conflating ownership and binary representation. A pointer to a region whose leaves all have zero physical size is represented like a pointer to the empty region: its address is the base of the allocation of the effective anchor of its authority, and that allocation is its provenance.
3. **Initialization:** relate `Uninit`, `Init`, and `Moved` to concrete values and representations; an authority `store` must correspond to writing an actual reference into **a single logical leaf** with an appropriate representation.
4. **Allocation and deallocation:** relate `alloc` / `free` to `AllocStep` / `DeallocStep`, justify `Satisfiable`, `Deallocable`, and `FreeCompat`, as well as the zero-physical-size case.
5. **Lifetimes:** relate `endUse`, `exitFrame`, `NoDangling`, dependencies, and death markers to the validity effects on actual storage.
6. **Pinning and static storage:** prove compatibility of permitted moves and pinned-address restrictions; specify the physical obligations of statics and external use. Hardware-specific MMIO semantics remain outside the sequential kernel.
7. **Arenas:** show that the library abstraction's derived operations and metadata, distinct from `S₃`, can be realized by operations O1–O16; relate issued regions and local/static/allocated storage to the elementary memory machine without reintroducing access after invalidation.
8. **`noalias`:** infer no pointer-lowering property from abstract invariants alone; memory justification is established here and the translation choices at Spec 13 level.

# XVIII. Examples of Semantic Behavior

The fragments below are **traces of abstract operations**, not language syntax. The judgments illustrate normative rules; they create no exception to the detailed preconditions.

## 83. Address Reuse and Old Provenance

An allocation `a` is created and an access retains its provenance; after deallocation, a new allocation `b` may occupy the same address. `a ≠ b` as abstract identities: reading through the old access is invalid even if the addresses are equal. A new valid access with provenance `b` may be used within its rights.

## 84. Partial Initialization and Reading

A valid write to a subrange initializes its corresponding bytes. Reading another subrange that remains uninitialized is not permitted. The correspondence for logical state `Init` must guarantee a representation valid for the expected type; the mere presence of bits does not authorize type confusion.

## 85. Splitting a Structure or SoA Columns

Starting from a `Modify` authority exercised over a structure, `split` may provide `Modify` authorities over disjoint leaf regions. Modification of each region is permitted as long as the other validity and holder conditions hold; a second independent derivation over the same leaf does not become legal merely by having a distinct name.

## 86. Arena, Active Views, and Reset

Two disjoint issued regions may be used simultaneously with valid derived rights. `reset` is rejected while an issuance or active dependency would make recycling unsafe; after a legal end of use for all the relevant blocks, the region may be reissued. Reissuance modifies neither the bytes nor the initialization state. A read remains subject to the ordinary conditions of the memory model, notably `Init`, access rights, and representation validity for the requested type. Spec 4 will determine the construction and typing obligations of reissued values.

## 87. Pinning an In-Place Value

A pinned in-place leaf cannot be physically moved by `transfer`. If only an allocation owned by a value is pinned, transfer of that value may remain valid when the other conditions hold, because the owned allocation is not physically moved.

## 88. Local Self-Blocking and Indirect Cycles

/-- Address of the reference to the region of authority `a` in `s2`: for a region whose leaves all
have zero physical size, the empty region included, the base of the allocation of the effective
anchor (§82.2, last sentence); otherwise the lowest address among the leaves of the region with a
nonzero size (lowest-address rule, recorded for §82.3). -/
def ptrAddr (s2 : Machine.State) (L : Layout) (s3 : S3) (a : Nat) : Nat :=
  match (s3.afp a).filter (fun l => decide (0 < (L l).len)) with
  | l :: ls => minOver (leafAddr s2 L) (leafAddr s2 L l) ls
  | [] => baseOf s2 (anchorAlloc L s3 a)

/-- The raw operation realizing `store(authority, target)` (§82.2, §82.3, §65): one write into the
range of the leaf `target` of the reference to the region of the authority, with the address of
`ptrAddr` and the provenance of the allocation of its effective anchor (§82.2). -/
def storeOps {Ty : Type} (pe : PtrEnc) (s2 : Machine.State) (L : Layout) (ty : Nat → Ty) (s3 : S3)
    (a p : Nat) : List (Machine.Op Ty) :=
  writeOps s2 L ty (fun _ => pe.enc (ptrAddr s2 L s3 a) (some (anchorAlloc L s3 a))) [p]

/-- The target of an `ok` `store` is a leaf of a usable place (§65.2). -/
theorem store_target {s3 : S3} {a p : Nat} (hpre : StorePre s3 a p) : LeafOfUsable s3 p :=
  ⟨p, List.mem_range.2 hpre.usable.lt, hpre.usable,
    mem_footprint.2 ⟨hpre.usable.lt, hpre.leaf, hpre.usable.lt, .inl rfl⟩⟩

/-- Realization of `store` (§82 preamble, §82.2, §82.3, §65, §16): under `Repr`, `WF3`, an `ok`
step of `store(authority, target)` and the parametric obligations of the write, the write of the
reference into the range of `target` is an `ok` raw step, and `Repr` holds after the step. Every
region has a reference address (§82.2). -/
theorem r6_store {Ty : Type} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {ty : Nat → Ty} {pe : PtrEnc} {L : Layout} {rtok : Nat → Nat}
    {s3 s3' : S3} {s2 : Machine.State} {a p : Nat} (hR : Repr L rtok s3 s2) (hw : WF3 s3)
    (h : StoreStep a p s3 (.ok s3'))
    (hob : OblAlong ObR ObW s2 (storeOps pe s2 L ty s3 a p)) :
    Machine.Exec C ObR ObW (storeOps pe s2 L ty s3 a p) s2 (run s2 (storeOps pe s2 L ty s3 a p)) ∧
      Repr L rtok s3' (run s2 (storeOps pe s2 L ty s3 a p)) := by
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  simp only [storeOps] at hob ⊢
  refine writes_repr hR hw (fun l hl => by rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hl]; exact store_target hpre)
    hob ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ <;> unfold storeEff <;> split
  · rfl
  · rfl
  · rfl
  · rfl
  · rfl
  · rfl
  · intro l hl
    dsimp only at hl
    split at hl
    · exact .inr (List.mem_singleton.2 ‹_›)
    · exact .inl hl
  · exact fun l hl => .inl hl


/-- An element without link of `i :: chain` is the last element of that chain (§42, §44: the
effective anchor is the root reached along the origin chain). -/
theorem chainF_last {org : Nat → Option Nat} :
obligation of the encoding for that reference, the range of `target` after the write decodes to
`ad` and carries the provenance of the allocation of the effective anchor. Every leaf of the region
lies in that allocation, which is live and contains the range of the leaf. For a region whose
leaves all have zero physical size, the empty region included, `ad` is the base of that allocation
(§82.2); otherwise `ad` is the address of a leaf of nonzero size of the region, the lowest among
them (lowest-address rule). -/
theorem pointer_sound_store {Ty : Type} {ty : Nat → Ty} {pe : PtrEnc} {L : Layout}
    {rtok : Nat → Nat}
    {s3 s3' : S3} {s2 : Machine.State} {a p ad : Nat} (hR : Repr L rtok s3 s2) (hw : WF3 s3)
    (hnd : NoDangling s3) (h : StoreStep a p s3 (.ok s3')) (had : ptrAddr s2 L s3 a = ad)
    (hsz : (L p).len = pe.size) (henc : PtrEncAt pe ad (some (anchorAlloc L s3 a))) :
    pe.decode (bytesOf (run s2 (storeOps (Ty := Ty) pe s2 L ty s3 a p)) L p) = ad ∧
      (∀ i, i < (L p).len →
        (bytesOf (run s2 (storeOps (Ty := Ty) pe s2 L ty s3 a p)) L p i).2 =
          some (anchorAlloc L s3 a)) ∧
      (∀ l ∈ s3.afp a, (L l).alloc = anchorAlloc L s3 a ∧
        AllocP s2 (L l).alloc fun al => al.live = true ∧ (L l).off + (L l).len ≤ al.size) ∧
      ((∀ l ∈ s3.afp a, (L l).len = 0) → ad = baseOf s2 (anchorAlloc L s3 a)) ∧
      ((∃ l ∈ s3.afp a, 0 < (L l).len) → ∃ l ∈ s3.afp a, 0 < (L l).len ∧ ad = leafAddr s2 L l ∧
        ∀ l' ∈ s3.afp a, 0 < (L l').len → ad ≤ leafAddr s2 L l') := by
  obtain ⟨hpre, -⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  obtain ⟨hpP, hpf, hpu⟩ := leaf_of_leafOfUsable hw (store_target hpre)
  obtain ⟨pa, hpa, -⟩ := hR.leaf_live hw hpP hpf hpu
  have hrun : run s2 (storeOps (Ty := Ty) pe s2 L ty s3 a p) =
      s2.write (leafAcc s2 L .write p) (pe.enc ad (some (anchorAlloc L s3 a))) := by
    simp only [storeOps, had, writeOps, List.map_cons, List.map_nil, run, opEff]
  have hbytes : ∀ i, i < (L p).len →
      bytesOf (run s2 (storeOps (Ty := Ty) pe s2 L ty s3 a p)) L p i =
      pe.enc ad (some (anchorAlloc L s3 a)) i := fun i hi => by
    rw [hrun]; exact bytesOf_write ⟨pa, hpa, trivial⟩ hi
  have hy : ∃ y, s3.A[a]? = some y ∧ y.active = true := by
def ParamsOK {Ty : Type} (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (π : Params Ty) : Prop :=
  PlacementOK π.pl ∧ GeomOK π.geom ∧ ∀ r, C (π.rtok r) (π.rtok r)

/-- The raw operations realizing a kernel step from `s3`, the memory state being `s2` (§82
preamble; §82.2–§82.5): computed from the parameters and the two states, nothing chosen per
step. -/
def opsOf {Ty : Type} (π : Params Ty) : KOp → S3 → Machine.State → List (Machine.Op Ty)
  | .transfer src dst, s3, s2 => transferOps π.L π.ty s2 s3 src dst
  | .enter _ ls, s3, s2 => allocOps π.pl π.geom π.rtok s3.P.length s2 (rootIdx ls.toShape)
  | .exit, s3, _ => exitOps π.L π.rtok s3
  | .read _ ls, _, s2 => readOps s2 π.L π.ty ls
  | .write _ ls w, _, s2 => writeOps s2 π.L π.ty w ls
  | .writeShared _ ls w, _, s2 => writeOps s2 π.L π.ty w ls
  | .free p auth, _, _ => freeOps π.L p auth
  | .alloc _ _ ls, s3, s2 => allocOps π.pl π.geom π.rtok s3.P.length s2 (rootIdx ls.toShape)
  | .store a p, s3, s2 => storeOps π.pe s2 π.L π.ty s3 a p
  | _, _, _ => []

/-- Obligations of one step (§20.3, §82): the parametric obligations of its reads and writes
(§20.3, §15, §16); the layout of new places (`enterFrame`, `alloc`, §82.1, §23 `LayoutWF`); the
instantiation of `K.FreeCompat` on the deallocation compatibility of the machine (`free`, §80,
§70.2, §82.4). -/
def StepObl {Ty : Type} (k : K) (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty)
    (ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty) (π : Params Ty) (op : KOp) (s3 : S3) (s2 : Machine.State) :
    Prop :=
  OblAlong ObR ObW s2 (opsOf π op s3 s2) ∧
    match op with
    | .enter _ ls => NewLayout π.L (enterP s3 ls) s3.P.length s2.next π.geom (rootIdx ls.toShape)
    | .alloc _ ow ls => NewLayout π.L (allocP s3 ow ls) s3.P.length s2.next π.geom
        (rootIdx ls.toShape)
    | .free p auth => k.FreeCompat p auth → FreeCompatInst C π.rtok p auth
    | _ => True

/-- Realization of every kernel step (§82 preamble, R6): under the obligations of the parameters,
`Repr`, `WF3` and `NoDangling` (parts of the kernel invariant `KInv`, §57) and the obligations of
the step, the raw operations of the step form an execution of `ok` raw steps, and `Repr` holds
after the step. -/
theorem r6 {Ty : Type} {k : K} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {π : Params Ty} {op : KOp} {s3 s3' : S3} {s2 : Machine.State}
    (hπ : ParamsOK C π) (hR : Repr π.L π.rtok s3 s2) (hw : WF3 s3) (hnd : NoDangling s3)
    (h : OpStep k op s3 s3') (hob : StepObl k C ObR ObW π op s3 s2) :
    Machine.Exec C ObR ObW (opsOf π op s3 s2) s2 (run s2 (opsOf π op s3 s2)) ∧
      Repr π.L π.rtok s3' (run s2 (opsOf π op s3 s2)) := by
  obtain ⟨hpl, hg, htc⟩ := hπ
  obtain ⟨hob, hx⟩ := hob
  cases op with
  | derive => exact ⟨.nil _, r6_derive hR h⟩
  | split => exact ⟨.nil _, r6_split hR h⟩
  | release => exact ⟨.nil _, r6_release hR h⟩
  | transfer => exact r6_transfer hR hw h hob
  | depend => exact ⟨.nil _, r6_depend hR h⟩
  | enter => exact r6_enter hR hw h hpl hg hx
  | exit =>
    have := r6_exit (ObR := ObR) (ObW := ObW) hR hw h htc
    exact ⟨this.1, this.2.2⟩
  | read =>
    have := r6_read (C := C) hR hw h hob
    exact ⟨this.1, this.2.2⟩
  | write => exact r2_write hR hw h hob
  | writeShared => exact r2_writeShared hR hw h hob
  | pin => exact ⟨.nil _, r6_pin hR h⟩
  | unpin => exact ⟨.nil _, r6_unpin hR h⟩
  | endUse => exact ⟨.nil _, r6_endUse hR h⟩
  | free =>
    have := r6_free (ObR := ObR) (ObW := ObW) hR hw hnd h hx
    exact ⟨this.1, this.2.2⟩
  | alloc => exact (r6_alloc hR hw h hpl hg hx).2
  | store => exact r6_store hR hw h hob

/-! ## Simulation (§82 preamble) -/

/-- Runs of the kernel from `S3.init statics` translated into the memory machine, with the
contract `K`, the deallocation compatibility `C`, the obligations `ObR`, `ObW` and the parameters
`π` fixed once for the run (§20.3 ¶3, §82): the initial state with the creations and writes of the
statics (`repr_init`); then each `ok` kernel step under its obligations (`StepObl`), followed by
its raw operations. No invariant is assumed on the states of the run: they are reachable, so the
kernel invariant holds on them (§57, `Access.reachable_kinv`). -/
inductive SimRun {Ty : Type} (k : K) (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty)
    (ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty) (statics : Statics) (π : Params Ty) :
    S3 → Machine.State → Prop where
  | init : StaticsOK statics →
      NewLayout π.L (S3.init statics).P 0 0 π.geom (rootIdx (statics.map (·.1))) →
      OblAlong ObR ObW (run Machine.State.empty (allocOps (Ty := Ty) π.pl π.geom π.rtok 0
        Machine.State.empty (rootIdx (statics.map (·.1))))) (writeOps (run Machine.State.empty
          (allocOps (Ty := Ty) π.pl π.geom π.rtok 0 Machine.State.empty
            (rootIdx (statics.map (·.1))))) π.L π.ty π.ival (initLeaves statics)) →
      SimRun k C ObR ObW statics π (S3.init statics)
        (run Machine.State.empty (initOps π.pl π.geom π.rtok π.L π.ty π.ival statics))
  | step {op : KOp} {s3 s3' : S3} {s2 : Machine.State} : SimRun k C ObR ObW statics π s3 s2 →
      OpStep k op s3 s3' → StepObl k C ObR ObW π op s3 s2 →
      SimRun k C ObR ObW statics π s3' (run s2 (opsOf π op s3 s2))

/-- The statics of a translated run are well formed (§47; `SimRun.init`). -/
theorem SimRun.staticsOK {Ty : Type} {k : K} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {statics : Statics} {π : Params Ty} {s3 : S3}
    {s2 : Machine.State} (h : SimRun k C ObR ObW statics π s3 s2) : StaticsOK statics := by
  induction h with
  | init hst _ _ => exact hst
  | step _ _ _ ih => exact ih

/-- Simulation (§82 preamble, §57, §9 ¶9): under `DDSound(K)` (§80), for every translated run, the
memory state is reached from the empty state by an execution of `ok` raw steps, it is related to
the kernel state by `Repr` (admissibility included), and the kernel state is reachable from
`S3.init statics` by the kernel steps O1–O16. -/
theorem simulation {Ty : Type} {k : K} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {statics : Statics} {π : Params Ty} {s3 : S3}
    {s2 : Machine.State} (hdd : DDSound k) (hπ : ParamsOK C π)
    (h : SimRun k C ObR ObW statics π s3 s2) :
    (∃ ops, Machine.Exec C ObR ObW ops Machine.State.empty s2) ∧ Repr π.L π.rtok s3 s2 ∧
      Access.Reachable k statics s3 := by
  have hst := h.staticsOK
  induction h with
  | init hst hlay hob =>
    obtain ⟨hex, hR⟩ := repr_init (C := C) hst hπ.1 hπ.2.1 hlay hob
    exact ⟨⟨_, hex⟩, hR, .init⟩
  | step _ hs hob ih =>
    obtain ⟨⟨ops, hex⟩, hR, hr⟩ := ih
    have hk := reachable_kinv hdd hst hr
    obtain ⟨hex', hR'⟩ := r6 hπ hR hk.1 hk.2.1.2.2 hs hob
    exact ⟨⟨_, exec_append hex hex'⟩, hR', .step hr hs.kstep⟩
